name: roster
description: List this session's delegated children (the roster): each entry's harp (agent_id), current run_id, state, latest report summary, and last activity. Terminal (ended) children are included only with include_terminal.

agent.description: agent_id and runner_id are coordinator-assigned and validated against the connection credential — never self-claimed by the agent process.

runner_id.description: which runner hosts this agent's process

mcp_servers.description: mcp_servers are the child's resolved MCP server NAMES ONLY (F1) — never command, args, or env, which can carry a secret. Composed strictly from the child's OWN resolved profile set (prodSpawner.childMCPServers), so this is the privilege-scoping audit trail: a real operator can confirm a run received exactly these servers, never a sibling's or the parent's. Empty for a run journaled before F1.

parent_run_id.description: Empty for a depth-1 (top-level) child; set for a depth-2+ grandchild (D5) — the SPAWNING run's run_id, so a roster consumer can render the delegation tree without re-deriving it from the event log.

permission_mode.description: permission_mode is the child's resolved permission mode's kind name (agent.PermissionMode.String(): "bypass"|"plan"|"default"| "acceptEdits"), fixed at enqueue (F1). Empty for a run journaled before F1.

phase.description: The run's current state, one of exactly: "queued" | "executing" | "parked" | "idle" | "ended". These five strings are the whole vocabulary; "ended" is the only terminal one, and entries in it appear only when include_terminal is set. Produced from the roster fold's state (coord/folds.go), which a test pins this list against (the documented vocabulary used to name an enum nothing constructs, so a consumer matching it never matched a single run).
